newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: COLUMBIANS IN SYDNEY COURT OVER DRUG HAUL
Four people, including two Columbians, are expected to appear in courts today charged in New South Wales over a cocaine importation racket.

The arrests at the weekend was the culmination of a 13-month investigation into the alleged syndicate's activities by the National Crime Authority, Federal Police and New South Wales Drug Enforcement Agency.
The arrests occured in Sydney and at a property at Tallong near Goulburn in the state's south, where a laboratory had been set up.
The NCA says the cocaine has been imported into Australia in impregnated plastic sheets.
Three people are appearing in court in Goulburn and one man in Sydney.
NSW SOUTH COAST COUNCIL SAYS IT IS NOT RACIST
A council on the south coast of New South Wales is moving today to head off any suggestion that it might be racist.
The Bega Valley Shire Council has been accused of fuelling the racism debate, because it has twice refused to support the Federal Government's bi-partisan declaration on human rights.
It maintained it had nothing to do with local government.
Following an angry reaction from Aboriginal leaders, the Mayor Tim Collins has now called a special meeting to set the record straight.
He says it will allow local residents a Christian and happy Christmas without the spectre of racism hanging over the shire.
WOMAN SENT TO JAIL FOR KILLING GRANDMOTHERS
A Sydney woman who battered her 86-year-old grandmother to death two and a half years ago, has been jailed for a minimum of seven years.
Magdala Lenaghan-Britton, who's been in custody for two years, pleaded guilty in the Supreme Court to the manslaughter of Doris Wennebom on the grounds of diminished responsibility.
Her husband Michael, who pleaded guilty to being an accessory, walked free.
The couple had been caring for Magdala's grandmother who was dying of cancer.

The court was told that during an argument, the woman lost control and pushed her grandmother's head against the wall and floor. Justice James said the grand daughter had been suffering a major psychiatric illness.
VICTORIAN LABOR PARTY VOTES ON A SPILL MOTION
The Victorian Labor Party caucus will be voting today on a spill of all positions including the party's leader.
The meeting was called by leader John Brumby who has announced that all party jobs, including his own, are up for grabs.
The spill follows a factional deal between the right wing Labor Unity group and some members of the left designed to revitalise the party.
Mr Brumby is expected to be returned as leader.
